newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius to replace sales tax with VAT.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius to replace sales tax with VAT.

text.p: Mauritius Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree said on Saturday that sales tax on goods would be replaced by value added tax (VAT) on goods and services.
Bunwaree said VAT was the cornerstone of reforms of indirect taxation on the Indian Ocean island. "The VAT system will improve tax buoyancy and promote investment activity," he added.
He said VAT would be introduced in the 1997-98 financial year after a campaign to raise public awareness.
He said sales tax on goods had drawbacks and the declining revenue from indirect taxes helped increase the budget deficit.
The deficit rose to 5.7 percent of gross domestic product in 1995-96 from 3.7 percent in 1994-95.
